tasks.task: Plan onboarding from signed to first useful result

items.when: When a deal has just closed and what was promised must reach the people who deliver
When you know what the customer bought and need the path to their first real result
When you want a second plan to compare, laid out in phases with milestones and owners
When the customer is a large account with several teams and sign-offs at each stage
When the plan has too many setup steps before the customer sees any value
When onboarding is live, to see each week where new customers stall in the first 30 days

tasks.task: Run the weekly account health report

items.when: Before scoring, to find blanks, duplicates and stale rows in the usage or billing export
Every week on the same day, to turn the latest signals into a short action list
When there is no score yet and you must build one from signals the business can see
When you have customer data and need a score, churn risk and upsell chance per account
When you want a second read on who is at risk from usage, engagement and ticket data
When the owner wants the weekly run to happen on its own with the next touch for each

tasks.task: Write a save plan for one at-risk customer

items.when: When the customer's recent messages hold warning signs you need named before you act
When an account turns amber or red and needs the reason, the owner and the next steps
When you want a second plan for the same account to compare with your own
When the risk comes from one open issue nobody owns
When the plan adds calls and gifts but does not remove the effort that annoys the customer

tasks.task: Write a welcome and onboarding email series

items.when: Before writing, to fix the first result each email should move the customer towards
When you need a 14-day email and text plan and a map of the first 100 days
When you want a second series with different timing and subject lines to compare
Before writing the series, to plan three different onboarding orders and draft each first email
When the emails give setup steps, to check each against the real product
Before sending, to cut each email to one action the customer can take

tasks.task: Plan renewals for one customer or a batch

items.when: When the contract has notice dates and terms you must read before you set the timeline
When a renewal date falls inside the planning window and the steps must run in order
When you need the timeline, risk notes and a value recap built only from real numbers
When you need every upcoming renewal listed with timing, risk and room to raise the price
When the client wants renewals due in 90 days flagged each month with a plan for each call
When one or two customers make up most of the revenue up for renewal

tasks.task: Write check-in messages for each customer stage

items.when: When you have the customer's last messages and need their mood before you write
When you need short, human check-ins for new, active, quiet and unhappy customers
When one customer's situation is unusual and needs a reply in a different tone to compare
When a check-in rambles, to cut it to one real reason to reply

tasks.task: Prepare a success plan or quarterly review pack

items.when: Before the meeting, to get a health read, value delivered and a draft agenda
When a key customer needs a 90-day plan or a review outline with talking points
When the account needs goals, key people, risks and next steps in one written plan
When the account is large and the plan must cover several buyers and open deals
When the customer's usage numbers need a clear point, proof and next step
When the review needs simple slides made from the outline
When the plan lists features used but not what the customer hired the product to do

tasks.task: Design a fair cancel flow with pause and downgrade options

items.when: When customers can only cancel by fighting for it, or leave with no other option shown
When you know the cancel reasons and what the billing tool can do, to match one save to each
When the flow lives in a subscription portal and failed payments need their own path
When you want a second flow with different save offers to compare
Before launch, to check the flow against cancellation rules where the business sells
When a save step starts to use pressure or guilt instead of an honest offer

tasks.task: Break down cancellations from a billing export

items.when: Before any sums, to find gaps, duplicates and odd values in the export
When you have a cancellation export and need who leaves, why and when with sums shown
When you need retention by sign-up month to see which groups leave early
When you want a score for where in the subscription life customers drop out
When the export has free-text cancel reasons that must be grouped into themes
When the client wants churn watched on a schedule after the first breakdown

tasks.task: Write a renewal email series

items.when: When notices must state the date, amount and how to cancel, with a value recap
When the renewal is an automatic charge and needs a reminder and a confirmation
When you want a second series with different timing and subject lines to compare
Before the renewal emails are written, to compare three orders for the reminders and the ask
When the emails quote a price or discount, to check every figure agrees
Before sending, to make sure each notice asks for one clear action

tasks.task: Announce a price change to customers

items.when: When the new price is not yet settled and the tiers need a second look first
When the price is set and customers need the date, the amount and their options stated plainly
When the notice is drafted, to predict the hard questions and try answers for each
Before sending, to check old and new prices and dates match everywhere they appear

tasks.task: Write win-back messages for customers who left

items.when: When members have left and you need honest messages matched to why each one went
When timing should follow how long buyers usually wait before they order again
When text or WhatsApp may work better than email, with consent rules kept
When win-back needs several messages, to plan three different approaches and draft each opener
Before sending, to cut each message to one offer and one way back

tasks.task: Write save scripts for phone, chat and email by cancel reason

items.when: Before the scripts, to pick the one fair save that fits each cancel reason
When the save desk needs words for each reason that still respect a no
When the member is angry as well as leaving and the script must name the feeling first
When a script offers a credit or a fix, to check each promise can be kept

tasks.task: Set customer tiers and service levels

items.when: When you have order history and need customers grouped by recency, frequency and spend
When every customer gets the same attention and the team cannot keep up
When the top tier should earn perks that are not discounts
When cutting service for small accounts saves cost now but may hurt what the firm is known for

tasks.task: Build a client intake form and document request list

items.when: Before the form, to list what sales already knows so the client is not asked twice
When you need questions aimed at what only the client knows
When the form is long and needs stages, conditional questions and save and resume
When intake ends in a kickoff and you need the brief, agenda and action list
When clients abandon the form, to cut fields and test the new flow

tasks.task: Write a setup guide and onboarding checklist

items.when: Before writing, to pick the few steps that lead to the first result and drop the rest
When you have product facts and customer problems and need short numbered routines
When setup questions keep coming and each needs its own searchable page
When the guide is drafted, to walk the product and fix steps and labels that differ

tasks.task: Write an upgrade offer for happy customers

items.when: When you need to see what an account owns, what it could add and the proof for each
Before any offer, to pick only the accounts healthy enough to hear one
When the upgrade needs value framing, terms and a name the customer understands
When the upgrade could be shown in the product at the right moment instead of by email
When the offer quotes a price or a saving, to check every figure is right

tasks.task: Reply to an unhappy customer and get the issue moving

items.when: When a hard message lands and you need its tone, urgency and warning signs read first
When the customer is angry and the reply must fix what it can and promise nothing false
When you want a second reply in a different tone to choose between
When the fix sits with another team and needs an escalation brief and a close-out
Before sending, to check the promises, facts and tone of your draft

tasks.task: Run a customer survey and sort the feedback

items.when: When you need a short survey or exit survey aimed at what you do not yet know
When the survey runs in a survey tool and you need its report or a list check before sending
When scores and open comments are in and need themes, trends and a short report
When feedback comes from tickets, surveys and calls and the loudest voice may mislead

tasks.task: Turn a customer call into notes and a follow-up

items.when: When you have call notes and need a follow-up email, a team summary and record updates
When the call was recorded and you also want coaching on how it went
When calls are recorded and you need searchable transcripts and action lists
When the follow-up repeats promises made on the call, to check each can be kept

tasks.task: Ask happy customers for a referral or a case study

items.when: When happy customers would refer others if there were a clear reward and a simple way
When a customer agrees to a case study and you need the outline and what they must approve
When you have quotes and results and need to know where each one works hardest

tasks.task: Map the customer journey from signed to renewal as steps

items.when: When the first step of the journey is a handoff that keeps losing details
When onboarding lives in one person's head and must become a written procedure
When time to first delivery is slow, to find the one stage holding everything up

always.when: Before any value recap or review goes out, to trace each number to the customer's own data
Before any message that promises a date, a credit or a fix

helpers.when: When the save plan depends on clearing open tickets or writing saved replies
When onboarding or win-back needs full automated flows built in an email tool
When a renewal or upgrade needs the price, tiers or discount rules worked out
When the health score or churn breakdown needs joined exports and tested sums
When onboarding needs a full set of help pages or a manual, not one setup guide
When the cancel flow or renewal notices must be checked against consumer rules by country

gaps: No library item writes check-in messages by customer stage; only the kit's prompt covers it
No library item writes save scripts for phone and chat by cancel reason, or lets you compare two script styles
No library item writes an exit survey with reason codes; the questionnaire writer is general
No library item writes a price rise announcement; the library can only check the figures in one
No library item builds a value recap for a renewal from the customer's own usage and results
No library item writes a sales-to-success handoff sheet or a document request list for a service firm
No library item sets service levels by customer tier for a business with 10 to 200 accounts
No library item asks a happy customer for a testimonial, review or reference call
No library item covers gym, studio or membership retention such as seasonal pause options
No library item checks a cancel flow against click-to-cancel and auto-renewal rules; only a general legal agent fits
No library item prepares the talk track for a renewal call from the seller's side
No library item maps the people in an account and plans for a champion leaving
